samples.question: This image shows five framed rectangular panels of identical size standing side by side in one row, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. Each panel contains a network of straight dark pipes laid on the same square lattice of nodes: every pipe runs either horizontally or vertically between two neighbouring lattice nodes, and pipes touch one another only end to end at a shared node, so no pipe ever crosses over or under another. Every panel contains exactly the same number of pipes and the same total length of gap, so the amount of ink, the number of pipes and the general clutter carry no information. In every panel exactly three of the pipes are broken: a broken pipe is drawn with a plainly visible empty gap in its middle, and no connection passes across that gap. Each panel also carries exactly two round terminal dots in a warm colour, each sitting on a lattice node where unbroken pipe ink meets, and in every panel the two terminals stand the same lattice distance apart, so their spacing and their placement inside the panel carry no information. Two terminals count as joined only if you can travel from one to the other along a continuous unbroken chain of pipe ink, following the pipes, never jumping across a gap and never crossing empty background. In exactly one panel the two terminals are joined. In each of the other four panels every possible route between the two terminals is interrupted by at least one visible gap, and the narrowest gap that would have to be bridged there is at least twice the width of a pipe. Which numbered panel has its two terminal dots joined by a continuous unbroken chain of pipe? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.
